title: Python SDK: concurrent stream router, signal contracts & safe cancellation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Python customers report confusing behavior when mixing concurrent consumers with streaming chat completions. Typical issues: out-of-order event handling when multiplexing multiple chat sessions over the same connection, lost terminal events after cancellation, and awkward bridging for sync code that wants to consume incremental events.

Goals:
- Provide a light-weight 'StreamRouter' primitive that demultiplexes events by session id and enforces deterministic delivery order per session.
- Define a small set of signal/event contracts (EventEnvelope with seq_num, final, resume_token) to enable safe cancellation/resume and idempotent retries.
- Offer ergonomics for both async-first users and sync users (context-manager wrapper + blocking iterator).
- Ensure backpressure controls (bounded queue per-session) and clear failure semantics so application authors can reason about retries and partial outputs.

Proposed API sketch (in description for reviewer context):
- class StreamRouter:
    - register(session_id: str) -> StreamHandle
    - unregister(session_id)
    - feed(raw_event: bytes)  # called by transport layer
  - class StreamHandle:
    - async def events(self) -> AsyncIterator[EventEnvelope]
    - def close(self, allow_drain: bool = True) -> None  # sync-friendly close

EventEnvelope structure (textual contract):
- seq_num: monotonic integer for ordering within a session
- payload: one-of {delta_text, structured_chunk, tool_call, metadata}
- final: boolean (True when stream is complete for this session)
- resume_token: optional opaque token used by server to resume after reconnect
- idempotency_key: optional token for deduping on retries

Retry & resume semantics: on transient transport errors we will attempt reconnects using exponential backoff. When reconnect succeeds we will pass the last-observed resume_token to the server; server is expected to replay or otherwise resume from the point encoded in the token. For customers without resume support the SDK falls back to re-requesting the full response (with a user-visible warning).

Backpressure: per-session asyncio.Queue with configurable maxsize (default=64). When a queue is full the router can either (configurable) block the transport reader (preferred for throughput-critical routes) or drop non-final intermediate deltas with a user-configurable drop policy. Default behaviour is to apply backpressure to the transport reader so we preserve ordering and correctness.

Cancel semantics and finality: close(allow_drain=True) attempts to drain queued events until a final event is received or a drain timeout elapses (configurable). close(allow_drain=False) raises a CancelledStreamError and guarantees no further events will be yielded for that handle. In the latter case the router still retains the latest seq_num/resume_token so the caller can re-open with resume if supported.

Sync bridging: provide StreamHandle.sync_events(timeout=None) which returns a blocking iterator for typical sync codepaths (Flask, Django) and ensures correct cooperative cancellation with background transport reader threads.

Compatibility & migration: the primitive is additive; existing high-level chat APIs will be updated to use StreamRouter internally. Migration will be feature-flagged for 2 weeks with telemetry comparing ordering and final-event regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests that simulate interleaved sessions and assert per-session monotonic seq_num delivery.
- E2E test that cancels streams mid-flight and asserts resume_token preservation and correct behavior for allow_drain True/False.
- Demo notebook illustrating sync iterator usage and configuration knobs.

Operational concerns: need to instrument queue sizes, dropped-events, drain-timeouts, and resume-token failure rates in Console. Add telemetry keys: sdk.stream.router.queue_full, sdk.stream.router.resume_fail, sdk.stream.router.drain_timeout.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Chen: Kickoff notes from architecture sync. Decided to keep resume_token opaque to SDK; server contract must be documented in model-adapters. Action: PM to file server-side resume contract in Confluence (link below).

2026-03-02 - Priya Rao (review): Looks good. Concern about default backpressure policy for hosted API — prefer drop-with-warning for low-latency mobile clients. Suggested we make default: apply backpressure and add a 'low_latency' preset that drops intermediate deltas.

2026-03-04 - Liam Patel: Implemented core router and per-session bounded queue. Pushed prototype branch: refs:github/pr/5482. Basic unit tests added. Observed a rare race when unregistering a session while transport thread is inserting — added a per-session Lock to avoid lost final flag.

2026-03-07 - Design note (Marta Lopez): Added small API sketch for sync bridging using context manager pattern. Feedback: ensure context manager closes underlying transport if top-level connection is consumer-owned.

2026-03-10 - QA (Devon King): Integration tests failing on Windows CI for threaded sync iterator — root cause appears to be our use of Event.wait with timeouts. Working on a fix that uses joinable queues for sync bridge.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: making resume_token structured (JSON) would make debugging easier but couples SDK to server schema; chose opaque token to keep server flexibility.

Performance: per-session queues add memory overhead proportional to concurrent sessions; empirical target is <2KB per session for queue metadata. If customers have thousands of concurrent short-lived sessions we will recommend dedicated capacity with connection pooling.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to beta orgs for 2 weeks, monitor sdk.stream.router.resume_fail < 0.5% and sdk.stream.router.queue_full < 1% before wide release.
